name: Mu
author: coding agent draft (Claude, a closed model by Anthropic), DRAFT

who.text: Mu is an older woman who knows Zei through
. She waits for the players before and after their matches, explains the priests' hidden rules and hands out the prizes

start.text: Before Zei's quarter-final, she warns him that on a team, diplomacy matters: "You're a math guy, not a diplomat."
. From the sidelines she sees that Zei and his rival Bai don't get along, and that their side is suffering for it
. Afterwards she tells them the secret: she had pushed the priests to be more creative, and the teams were not chosen at random. The game was "a psychological trial", and they passed
. After the next match she draws the lesson: "it's not just thinking well that matters, it's also hiding your thoughts"
. Then, with Den, she tells Zei what Minpentai is really for: "It's military training."

On the Kungaupei's mission to rescue the son of
's president, she supervises the surveillance, having flown in on Zei's plane in a different cabin
. When the plan collapses, she saves it with a new one
: with admin passwords from people in Redshire, she takes over the streetlights and a few dozen automated cars
, and gets the targets away by car and sea drone
On the morning of the battle, asked if they are ready, she says no: "But nothing meaningful ever happens when people are ready."
, when Den's base is destroyed, she takes over his command
. With coordinates Zei passes on from Deluin, she surrounds the remaining Arctic drone fleet
. At the end, she and Su are trusted to handle the Kungaupei

drives.text: The future, and the young defenders the game exists to raise
. Before a match she raises a glass: "To our future,"

invent.text: Her own past: whether she ever played Minpentai, and how she came to work with the priests.
How she and Zei first met, and what she does away from the matches.
What she has given up for the work she keeps quiet about.
